What happens to my game libraries (Steam, GOG, Epic, PlayStation, Xbox) when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026

Short answer: In most cases your digital games can't be passed on. Steam, Epic, PlayStation and Xbox license games to you personally and say the licence isn't transferable. Family can usually only stop charges or close the account. Write down what you own, and keep saves or mods backed up separately.

Key facts

  • Steam: licences, not transferable (Subscriber Agreement)
  • Epic: personal, non-transferable licence; account can't be given away
  • PlayStation (AU): licence not transferable unless local law requires
  • Xbox: personal, non-transferable licence to currency and virtual goods
  • GOG: no official bereavement policy we could verify

How do I prepare my game libraries (Steam, GOG, Epic, PlayStation, Xbox) account?

  1. Write down which stores you use (Steam, GOG, Epic, PlayStation, Xbox) and the email on each account.
  2. Store logins in a password manager with emergency access so someone can cancel subscriptions and close accounts.
  3. Back up local saves, screenshots and mods you care about outside the store.
  4. After a death: cancel subscriptions such as Game Pass or PlayStation Plus through the account or the payment card.
  5. Contact each store's support with a death certificate to ask about closure. Don't expect the games library to be transferred.

Read the official policy ↗

What can't be recovered?

  • Purchased game libraries (licences end with the account)
  • Wallet balances and in-game currency
  • Cloud saves if the account is closed

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my game libraries (Steam, GOG, Epic, PlayStation, Xbox) when I die?

In most cases your digital games can't be passed on. Steam, Epic, PlayStation and Xbox license games to you personally and say the licence isn't transferable. Family can usually only stop charges or close the account. Write down what you own, and keep saves or mods backed up separately.

Can I leave my Steam library to someone?

Steam's Subscriber Agreement says subscriptions are licences, Valve doesn't recognise transfers outside Steam (including by operation of law), and subscriptions aren't transferable.

What about Epic Games?

Epic's terms say your licence is personal and non-transferable, and you can't sell, give away or trade your Epic Games Account.

What about PlayStation?

PlayStation's Australian terms say your licence to use Digital Products is not transferable unless local law says it must be.

What about Xbox?

The Microsoft Services Agreement gives you a personal, non-transferable licence to Xbox game currency and virtual goods. Microsoft accounts are closed automatically after two years of inactivity if no one can sign in.

What about GOG?

We couldn't verify a published GOG bereavement policy from an official source. Contact GOG Support with a death certificate.
